#: packages collector: the manager this host has, and that manager's rows. A variant stages exactly the one payload its manager names — dpkg.json here — so this manifest covers the union of the shapes captured so far, not the union of the shapes the collector can read.
#rows: dpkg-query is asked for four fields in an order this collector chose (adapters/packages.py DPKG_FORMAT), so a row is a fixed 4-tuple and each index is classified by what it IS rather than by shape: 0 name, 1 version, 2 architecture, 3 the db status. rpm's rows are the same idea one field shorter; a capture from an rpm host would take its own `*.0`/`*.1`/`*.2` entries here, and none exists yet to classify.
#nothing: A package's name, version and architecture come out of a distribution archive: the same strings on every machine that installed the same thing, and identical for every reader who runs `apt install` after them. THE BOUND IS STATED because it is a decision and not a shape — a locally built or estate-private package carries a name somebody in this estate chose, which is content and would belong on the free-text pass. No such package is in the committed capture; a capture that had one would move these entries, not survive them.
#manager: manager.json is a JSON document whose whole content is one scalar — the string "dpkg", which is what _detect returned. It carries no leaf a dotted path can name, and se-anonymise's `whole` entries are reserved for payloads that are not JSON at all, so this manifest CANNOT yet classify it and a scrub run over that file refuses at `(root)`. That refusal is the tool behaving correctly and the manifest being unable to answer it; the classification, stated here for a reader and for whoever repairs the grammar, is `nothing` — the value is one of the three manager names this collector can return, and it is the same word on every machine that has that manager.
#nixstore: A capture from a NixOS host stages nixstore.json, a flat {name-version: /nix/store/<hash>-<name-version>} map whose ROOT KEYS are data — the same shape as storage's devlinks, so it would take payload-scoped `~key` and `*` entries. No such capture is committed, and classifying a payload nobody has captured would be a decision made without the document in front of it.
